common_confusions: BC-MIS-05001 (hypotheses treated as decoration, with the conclusion taken to be the whole theorem)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any conclusion is written, the learner names continuity on the closed interval [a,b] and differentiability on the open interval (a,b) as the two conditions the Mean Value Theorem demands, keeps the closed and open endpoints distinct in the interval notation, and does this whether the function arrives as a formula, a table, or a verbal statement of differentiability. No response shows BC-ERR-05001 (conclusion used with no mention of continuity or differentiability) or BC-ERR-99008 (a theorem applied without its hypotheses established first).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conditions appear only when asked for, which is what BC-SIG-05001 records, correct arithmetic and a correct conclusion with no sentence establishing continuity or differentiability. Another intermediate state names one condition and drops the other, or names both but attaches them to the wrong interval type, and the 2013 Q3 part B scoring behaviour of hypotheses never stated with the average rate correct shows the same partial hold, an instance of BC-ERR-05001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Wrong open or closed endpoints in the stated conditions point back at BC-PRQ-05004 (interval notation and the open versus closed distinction), and a learner who cannot say that differentiability at a point gives continuity there has not secured BC-SKL-02019, the tell being a response that lists differentiability twice rather than listing continuity on [a,b] and differentiability on (a,b).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05001 (an existence theorem is licensed by its conditions, not by its name); a procedural failure in the endpoint notation points instead to BC-PRQ-05004 (open versus closed interval notation)

skills.description_formal: Name continuity on the closed interval and differentiability on the open interval as the conditions the Mean Value Theorem requires.
skills.description_plain: Say what must be true of the function before the theorem may be used.
skills.name: State the hypotheses of the Mean Value Theorem for a function and an interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05001 (hypotheses treated as decoration, with the conclusion taken to be the whole theorem)
BC-MIS-05002 (writing the name of a theorem taken to complete the argument)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given that f is differentiable on an interval, the written work converts that into continuity explicitly, saying that f is continuous on [a,b] because it is differentiable there, and separately confirms differentiability on (a,b). The same conversion holds from a table, from a graph, and from a verbal hypothesis. BC-ERR-05002 (continuity asserted without being drawn from the given differentiability) is absent, as is BC-ERR-99008 (hypotheses skipped before the conclusion).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A bare sentence that f is continuous, with nothing behind it, is the characteristic middle state and it is exactly BC-ERR-05002, refused by the 2025 guideline. BC-SIG-05001 catches its quieter form, right arithmetic and right answer with no hypothesis sentence at all. The 2018 Q4 part B behaviour of differentiability never converted to continuity marks the same gap, and the 2021 Q4 part D behaviour of a theorem asserted with no hypotheses sits alongside it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the learner cannot list what the Mean Value Theorem requires in the first place, the failure belongs to BC-SKL-05001 rather than to the verification step, and the tell is a response that verifies some property of f that the theorem never asked for.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05002 (a justification has to convince a reader who has never heard of the theorem); a procedural failure, meaning the implication is known but never written down, points instead to BC-SKL-05001 (stating the hypotheses)

skills.description_formal: Given a statement that a function is differentiable, state that it is therefore continuous on the closed interval, and confirm differentiability on the open interval.
skills.description_plain: Check the given information really does supply continuity and differentiability.
skills.name: Verify that the hypotheses hold on the given interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05003 (average rate of change read as the average of the endpoint values)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
BC-QA-05002 (a function and a closed interval given, with the interior input where the instantaneous rate equals the average rate required)
adaptive.mastered_if: The quotient f(b) minus f(a) over b minus a is formed in that order, with the interval length as the denominator, and the value carries the units of a rate rather than the units of f. The learner produces it from a formula, from a table of values, and from a graph, and accepts the equivalent form of an integral of f prime over the interval divided by the interval length. Neither BC-ERR-05003 (endpoint values averaged, subtraction reversed, or division by the wrong difference) appears in any representation.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The setup is right on a formula but collapses on a table, or the subtraction order flips so the sign of the rate is wrong, both of them forms of BC-ERR-05003. The 2021 Q4 part D behaviour of a difference quotient with the wrong interval length is the arithmetic-setup version, and the 2025 Q1 part B behaviour of the average value of the function substituted for the average rate of change is the other, where the right machinery is aimed at the wrong quantity.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Reporting the mean of the two endpoint outputs, which BC-SIG-05002 flags, is a failure of BC-PRQ-05008 (average rate of change as a difference quotient) and not of this skill, and asking for the units of the computed number separates the two. Misreading f(t) or an evaluation at a stated input instead points at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05003 (a rate is a change in output divided by a change in input, checkable against the units of f prime); a procedural failure in the subtraction or the denominator points instead to BC-PRQ-05008 (forming the difference quotient)

skills.description_formal: Evaluate the quotient of f(b) minus f(a) over b minus a for the stated interval, from a formula, a table, or a graph.
skills.description_plain: Work out the change in output divided by the change in input across the interval.
skills.name: Compute the average rate of change over a closed interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05002 (writing the name of a theorem taken to complete the argument)
BC-MIS-05004 (an existence theorem read as naming the input rather than asserting one exists)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
adaptive.mastered_if: Three things sit in the same argument. The hypotheses are on the page, the average rate of change is computed, and the response then says yes, there is a c strictly between a and b with f prime of c equal to that rate, naming the Mean Value Theorem. The subject of every sentence is named, so f and f prime are never left to a pronoun. BC-ERR-05004 (arithmetic done but no affirmative answer and no theorem), BC-ERR-05002 (continuity not drawn from differentiability), and BC-ERR-99001 (vague referent such as it or the graph) are all absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Arithmetic and conclusion agree while the theorem named concerns values of the function rather than values of the derivative, which is BC-SIG-05003. Other middle states compute everything and stop short of the word yes or of the theorem's name, the shape of BC-ERR-05004, matching the 2013 Q3 part B behaviour of an average rate correct with the theorem unnamed and the 2018 Q4 part B behaviour of the same gap.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An unsupported continuity claim under the conclusion is BC-SKL-05002 failing rather than this one, and a wrong value for the average rate, with the existence sentence written correctly around it, belongs to BC-SKL-05003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05004 (existence is asserted, location is not); a procedural failure, where the affirmative sentence or the theorem name is simply missing from otherwise sound work, points instead to BC-ERR-05004 (writing the answer with its justification)

skills.description_formal: From the verified hypotheses and the computed average rate of change, assert the existence of c strictly between the endpoints with f'(c) equal to that rate, naming the theorem.
skills.description_plain: State that some interior point has instantaneous rate equal to the average rate, and say why.
skills.name: Conclude that a point with the average rate exists on the open interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05004 (an existence theorem read as naming the input rather than asserting one exists)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05002 (a function and a closed interval given, with the interior input where the instantaneous rate equals the average rate required)
adaptive.mastered_if: Setting f prime of x equal to the average rate of change, solving, and then keeping only the solutions strictly inside (a,b) is done as one movement, with the equation itself written out so the reported number is supported rather than bare. Endpoint solutions are discarded and said to be discarded. A calculator solve is backed by the equation on the page. BC-ERR-05005 (a reported value that is an endpoint or lies outside the interval) does not occur.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05004 describes the usual halfway point, a correct derivative equation with a reported input at an endpoint or outside the interval. A second pattern is the bare numerical value with no supporting equation, which the BC-QA-05002 scoring treats as earning neither point, and the 2025 Q1 part B behaviour of an equation solved with the setup never written is the same omission.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A wrong right-hand side in the derivative equation traces to BC-SKL-05003, since the average rate itself was formed wrongly, and an inability to isolate the roots of the resulting equation or to see where a denominator vanishes traces to BC-PRQ-05001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05004 (the theorem guarantees a c without telling you where it is, so the interval condition is yours to impose); a procedural failure in the algebra points instead to BC-PRQ-05001 (solving equations and locating where an expression is zero or undefined)

skills.description_formal: Solve f'(x) equal to the average rate of change over the interval and report the solutions that lie strictly inside it.
skills.description_plain: Set the derivative equal to the average rate and solve.
skills.name: Solve for a value of c that the theorem provides

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05002 (writing the name of a theorem taken to complete the argument)
BC-MIS-05005 (one existence theorem used for claims about function values and about derivative values alike)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
adaptive.mastered_if: Equal endpoint outputs are presented first, as f(a) equal to f(b) or as a difference of zero, the average rate of change is therefore zero, and the response concludes that some c in (a,b) has f prime of c equal to zero, with the Mean Value Theorem named and continuity drawn from differentiability. The claim is kept about the derivative, so the Intermediate Value Theorem never enters. Neither BC-ERR-05006 (Intermediate Value Theorem cited for a claim about the derivative) nor BC-ERR-05004 (no affirmative answer and no theorem) is present, in the table form or the graph form.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The endpoint equality is computed and the argument then reaches for the wrong existence theorem, BC-SIG-05003, arithmetic sound but the theorem cited concerning values of f. The 2023 Q1 part B behaviours give two more, a yes with no endpoint computation, guessed from the table's shape, and continuity asserted rather than derived, and both leave the second point out of reach because it depends on the first.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the endpoint difference itself is mishandled, the break is at BC-SKL-05003, and if the existence sentence is missing its structure rather than its theorem, the break is at BC-SKL-05004, the tell being that the zero average rate is stated correctly and nothing follows from it.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05005 (which theorem speaks about f and which speaks about f prime); a procedural failure, where the right theorem is named but the endpoint equality is never shown, points instead to BC-SKL-05003 (computing the average rate of change)

skills.description_formal: Show f(a) equal to f(b), hence an average rate of change of zero, and conclude the existence of an interior c with f'(c) equal to zero.
skills.description_plain: When the two endpoint outputs agree, argue that the derivative must be zero somewhere between them.
skills.name: Justify that a derivative takes a particular value using equal endpoint outputs

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05006 (continuity assumed available on any interval, so the closed interval check is skipped)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05010 (deciding whether a function is assured of attaining a largest and a smallest value on a closed interval, and saying why)
adaptive.mastered_if: One condition is named and it is the right one, continuity of f on the closed interval [a,b], with the closedness treated as part of the hypothesis rather than as incidental notation. Asked why an open interval will not do, the learner can produce a function on it with no largest value. BC-ERR-05007 (a maximum and a minimum claimed across a break or on an open interval), BC-ERR-05001 (hypotheses skipped before the conclusion is used), and BC-ERR-99008 (the same habit across theorems) are absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05005 captures the state in which the response says the function is continuous and offers nothing that establishes it. Differentiability is sometimes offered as the Extreme Value Theorem's condition, importing the Mean Value Theorem's hypothesis list, and the closed interval requirement is sometimes dropped while continuity is kept, which is the half of BC-ERR-05007 that concerns open intervals.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Writing the interval with the wrong endpoint type, so that the stated hypothesis quietly applies to (a,b), is a BC-PRQ-05004 failure about open versus closed notation rather than a misunderstanding of the theorem.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05006 (the closed interval is doing work in the hypothesis); a procedural failure confined to the notation points instead to BC-PRQ-05004 (open versus closed interval notation)

skills.description_formal: Name continuity on the closed interval [a,b] as the condition the Extreme Value Theorem requires.
skills.description_plain: Say that the function must be continuous on a closed interval.
skills.name: State the hypothesis of the Extreme Value Theorem

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05006 (continuity assumed available on any interval, so the closed interval check is skipped)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05010 (deciding whether a function is assured of attaining a largest and a smallest value on a closed interval, and saying why)
adaptive.mastered_if: Continuity on the whole of [a,b], endpoints included, is traced to something actually given, a stated differentiability claim, an unbroken graph, or an explicit statement of continuity, and the learner says which. A break inside the interval, or an interval that turns out to be open, is caught and the theorem is withheld. This holds from a graph, from an analytic description, and from a verbal hypothesis, with no instance of BC-ERR-05007 (the theorem invoked across a break or on an open interval) or BC-ERR-99008 (conclusion ahead of hypothesis).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Continuity is claimed with no source behind the claim, the state BC-SIG-05005 describes, or it is checked on the interior and left unchecked at the endpoints. A related middle state verifies continuity correctly but never says that the interval is closed, so half of the BC-QA-05010 hypothesis point is missing and the conclusion point that depends on it cannot follow.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A learner who does not know that continuity on a closed interval is the condition being checked is failing BC-SKL-05007, and the sign is a verification aimed at differentiability on the open interval instead.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05006 (a discontinuity anywhere in [a,b], including at an endpoint, removes the guarantee); a procedural failure, where the source of continuity is known but never cited, points instead to BC-SKL-05007 (stating the hypothesis)

skills.description_formal: Confirm from the given statement, graph, or differentiability claim that f is continuous on [a,b], including at both endpoints.
skills.description_plain: Check that the given information supplies continuity on the whole closed interval.
skills.name: Verify continuity on the closed interval before applying the theorem

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05006 (continuity assumed on any interval, so the theorem is applied to open intervals or across discontinuities)
BC-MIS-05007 (a relative extremum taken as an absolute extremum over the whole interval)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05010 (Extreme Value Theorem existence claim on a closed interval, deciding whether the largest and smallest values are assured and saying why)
adaptive.mastered_if: On a closed interval where continuity has already been established from the given information, the response asserts that f attains at least one minimum value and at least one maximum value there, names the Extreme Value Theorem as the warrant, and deliberately stops short of reporting any input. The existence sentence holds when the function arrives graphically as in BC-REP-04 and when it arrives as a table of values, and BC-ERR-05008, treating an existence theorem as though it named the location of the extremum, is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Continuity on the closed interval is checked and the theorem is named, yet the conclusion sentence never says that a minimum value and a maximum value are attained, matching BC-SIG-05006 where an input is offered in place of the existence claim. A second intermediate state has the conclusion right while the hypothesis is asserted rather than drawn from the given information, which in the shape used for the Mean Value Theorem existence part leaves the hypothesis point unearned. Partial traces of BC-ERR-05008 show up as an existence sentence followed by an unsupported location.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The conclusion is stated in the right words but the interval was never tested for closure or the function for continuity across it, which is BC-SKL-05008 missing rather than this skill. The tell is a theorem invoked on an open interval or across a jump with no sentence connecting the given information to continuity.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05006 (what the closed interval and continuity hypotheses actually buy) for the conceptual failure. A response that understands existence but still hands back an input points instead to BC-SKL-05008, where the hypothesis check is written out before the conclusion sentence.

skills.description_formal: From verified continuity on [a,b], assert that f attains at least one minimum value and at least one maximum value on that interval.
skills.description_plain: State that the function reaches a lowest and a highest value on the interval.
skills.name: Conclude that a minimum value and a maximum value exist

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05008 (a zero derivative read as the definition of a turning point, so no sign change is checked)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a justification covering the whole interval)
BC-QA-05007 (critical point located and classified for a function given through a differential equation or an accumulation function)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation f prime of x equal to zero appears on the page before any solution is listed, the solutions are screened against the domain of f so that an input where the function itself is undefined is dropped, and the surviving inputs are called critical points. This holds whether f is given by a formula as in BC-REP-01 or through a differential equation or accumulation relation where the derivative must first be written from the given relation, and neither BC-ERR-05009, zeros listed without the derivative condition shown, nor BC-ERR-05010, solutions outside the domain kept, is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Correct critical inputs arrive with no equation behind them, which is BC-SIG-05007 exactly and which forfeits the considering the derivative equal to zero point under the candidates test. Other intermediate states keep an input where the derivative expression vanishes but the function is undefined, that being BC-ERR-05010, or find the critical input and then never evaluate the function there, the location-versus-value split recorded in the 2013 and 2021 scoring commentary. A further partial state solves the equation correctly and then asserts an extremum with a purely local sign change, leaving the uniqueness statement out.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the derivative is correct but the algebra of setting a factored or rational expression to zero collapses, the failure is BC-PRQ-05001 and not this skill, recognisable by a lost root or a denominator zero mistaken for a solution. When every candidate the algebra produced is kept including one outside the domain, BC-PRQ-05003 is the gap, and where the derivative itself cannot be written from an accumulation relation the shortfall sits in BC-SKL-06021.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05008 (a critical point is a candidate, not a verdict) for the conceptual failure. Where the concept is intact and only the written setup or the domain screen is missing, the target is BC-PRQ-05001 together with BC-PRQ-05003.

skills.description_formal: Solve f'(x) equal to zero and retain the solutions that lie in the domain of f, presenting the equation rather than only the solutions.
skills.description_plain: Solve the derivative equal to zero and keep the solutions in the domain.
skills.name: Determine critical points where the first derivative equals zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05009 (the derivative assumed to exist wherever the function does, so corners, cusps and vertical tangents never appear)
BC-MIS-05008 (a zero derivative read as the definition of a turning point, so no sign change is checked)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a justification covering the whole interval)
adaptive.mastered_if: Corners, cusps and vertical tangents inside the domain of f are hunted for and added to the critical point list alongside the zeros of f prime, with the reason given in terms of f prime failing to exist there rather than being zero. The same sweep happens from a formula as in BC-REP-01 and from a plotted curve as in BC-REP-02, where a break in the derivative graph is marked, and BC-ERR-05011, omitting the inputs at which the derivative fails to exist, does not occur even when the candidates list is long.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Every zero of f prime is present and the corner or cusp is missing, which is BC-SIG-05008 and leaves the candidates list one short so the comparison can select the wrong extremum. A related intermediate state notices the corner but files it as an extremum without checking the sign of f prime on each side.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A response that cannot say where a radical or rational expression stops being defined is short on BC-PRQ-05003 rather than on this skill, and the sign is a candidate list restricted to a domain the student never wrote down. Failure to locate where the derivative expression is undefined at all points back to BC-PRQ-05001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05009 (differentiability is a stronger condition than existence of the function) for the conceptual failure. When the family of non-differentiable points is known but never located, the procedural target is BC-PRQ-05003, the domain analysis that says where such points can sit.

skills.description_formal: Locate inputs in the domain of f where f' is undefined, such as a corner, a cusp, or a vertical tangent, and include them among the critical points.
skills.description_plain: Find the domain inputs where the derivative does not exist.
skills.name: Determine critical points where the first derivative fails to exist

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05007 (a local high or low point taken as the largest or smallest value on the whole interval)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a justification covering the whole interval)
BC-QA-05010 (Extreme Value Theorem existence claim on a closed interval, deciding whether the largest and smallest values are assured and saying why)
adaptive.mastered_if: Asked about an extremum, the response says what set of inputs the value is being compared against, calling it relative when the comparison is with nearby values and absolute when it covers the whole interval, and it reads that distinction off a plotted curve as in BC-REP-02 as readily as off a described situation in BC-REP-04. A global claim is backed by a candidates table containing both endpoints and every interior critical point, so BC-ERR-05012, a relative extremum reported as the absolute one, and BC-ERR-99004, a local argument offered where a global argument was required, are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A relative extremum is identified correctly and then handed in as the answer to an absolute extremum question, which is BC-SIG-05009 and BC-ERR-05012 together, and the answer point may survive while the justification point does not. Nearby states run the candidates test but drop an endpoint or one interior critical point, which is BC-ERR-99004 in its incomplete-table form, or justify a global claim by a single sign change at one input.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the extremum cannot be picked off the plotted curve in the first place, or rises and falls are misread from the drawing, the gap is BC-PRQ-05006 rather than the relative versus absolute distinction. The sign is a classification argument applied confidently to a point the student located wrongly on the graph.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05007 (the comparison set is what separates a local claim from a global one) for the conceptual failure. Where the distinction is understood but the table is short, the procedural target is BC-QA-05006, carrying the candidates test through both endpoints and every interior critical point.

skills.description_formal: Given a described or plotted extremum, classify it as relative or absolute by the range of inputs against which the value is compared.
skills.description_plain: Say whether a claim is about nearby values or about the whole interval.
skills.name: Distinguish a relative extremum from an absolute extremum

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05008 (a zero derivative read as the definition of a turning point, so no sign change is checked)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (relative extremum classified from the behaviour of the first derivative, with the answer and its reason scored together)
adaptive.mastered_if: A case is produced or described in which f prime is zero at an input yet keeps the same sign immediately on both sides, and the response concludes neither a relative maximum nor a relative minimum, stating the absence of the sign change as the reason. The wording holds whether the derivative arrives as a formula in BC-REP-01 or as a plotted curve in BC-REP-02, intervals of positivity need not be written out for the reason to stand, and BC-ERR-05013, declaring an extremum at a critical point with no sign change, is nowhere in the work.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The classification comes out as neither while the reason is phrased as positive before and positive after without the sign-change criterion ever being named, so the single answer with reason point is at risk. In a weaker intermediate state, described by BC-SIG-05010 and BC-ERR-05013, a relative extremum is announced at an input where f prime holds its sign, and in another the reason is given about f rather than about f prime.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the input under discussion was never obtained by setting f prime equal to zero in the first place, BC-SKL-05010 is the missing piece, and the tell is an input asserted with no equation behind it before any sign question is raised.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05008 (the sign change, not the zero, is what makes an extremum) for the conceptual failure. Where the concept holds and only the reason sentence is missing its criterion, the target is BC-QA-05003, the answer-with-reason wording.

skills.description_formal: Exhibit or describe a critical point at which f' does not change sign, so that f has neither a relative maximum nor a relative minimum there.
skills.description_plain: Give a case where the derivative is zero but the function keeps going the same way.
skills.name: Explain why a critical point need not be a relative extremum

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05010 (increase and decrease decided from whether the function values are positive or negative)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05008 (intervals of increase or decrease supported by the sign of the named derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given f or f prime symbolically as in BC-REP-01, the zeros and the undefined points of f prime are found first, then the sign of f prime is settled on each resulting open interval, usually by a test value that gets written down. Intervals and reason are kept separate in the write-up, the reason naming f prime rather than restating the conclusion, and BC-ERR-05014, assigning the wrong sign on one interval of the chart, is absent across factored polynomial, rational and chain rule cases alike.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: All partition points are correct and one interval carries the wrong sign, which is BC-SIG-05011 and BC-ERR-05014 and which costs the reason point along with the intervals. Other intermediate work uses the sign of the quantity itself where the sign of its derivative was wanted, the direction-of-change confusion recorded in the 2019 and 2022 commentary, or omits the chain rule factor when a second derivative is built so the inner variable is never treated as a function of time.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the number line is partitioned wrongly because a factored or rational expression was not solved correctly, the failure is BC-PRQ-05001, and when the partition points are right but the sign on a piece cannot be determined the gap is BC-PRQ-05002. A derivative that is wrong before any sign work begins points back to BC-SKL-02027.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05010 (the sign of f prime, not the sign of f, drives increase and decrease) for the conceptual failure. A student who has that straight and still misassigns a sign needs BC-PRQ-05002, the number line sign analysis.

skills.description_formal: Given f or f' symbolically, find the zeros and undefined points of f' and determine the sign of f' on each resulting open interval.
skills.description_plain: Work out the sign of the derivative expression on each interval.
skills.name: Determine where the first derivative is positive or negative from a formula

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (questions about the function answered by reading whatever curve is drawn, even when the drawn curve is a derivative or an integrand)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05008 (intervals of increase or decrease supported by the sign of the named derivative)
BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives and identifying which is which)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before anything is reported, the drawn curve in BC-REP-02 is labelled as f prime and f is named as the function under discussion, after which the intervals where the plotted values sit above the axis are reported as intervals on which f increases and those below as intervals on which f decreases. Rising portions of the plotted curve are kept apart from portions above the axis, so BC-ERR-05016, confusing increase of the derivative with positivity of the derivative, does not creep in, and BC-ERR-05015, answering about the drawn curve as though it were f, does not appear even when a compound condition asks about both f and f prime at once.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The intervals handed back are the ones on which the drawn curve rises, which is BC-SIG-05012 and BC-ERR-05015 together and sends every dependent part to the wrong function. Half-answers to a compound condition, such as giving where f increases while leaving out that f prime is decreasing there, and reasons phrased about f where the referent had to be f prime, sit in the same band, as does reading concavity off the sign of the plotted curve.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Trouble extracting zeros, rises and falls from a plotted curve at all is BC-PRQ-05006 rather than a referent problem, and the tell is that the reported intervals do not match the drawing regardless of which function the student thinks it shows.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05011 (naming the plotted object before reading anything off it) for the conceptual failure. When the referent is right and the trouble is above the axis versus rising, the target is BC-SKL-05041 and the separation of positivity from increase.

skills.description_formal: From a plotted f', identify the intervals where the plotted values are positive and where they are negative, and report the corresponding behaviour of f.
skills.description_plain: Use where the derivative graph is above or below the axis.
skills.name: Read intervals of increase and decrease from the graph of the derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05012 (a gap in the domain treated as not interrupting an interval of behaviour)
BC-MIS-05010 (increase and decrease decided from whether the function values are positive or negative)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05008 (intervals of increase or decrease supported by the sign of the named derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: The number line is cut at the critical points of f and at every point of discontinuity, a vertical asymptote or a domain gap included, and a sign for f prime is recorded on each open piece with nothing claimed across a break. Reported intervals therefore stop at the gap instead of spanning it, the chart reads the same whether f arrives as a formula in BC-REP-01 or as a described situation in BC-REP-04, and BC-ERR-05017, partitioning at the zeros of the derivative alone while ignoring a domain gap, is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Signs are correct on every piece of a chart that was partitioned at the zeros of f prime only, so an interval spans an input where f does not exist, which is BC-ERR-05017. A weaker intermediate state splits the line at the zeros of f rather than of f prime, matching BC-SIG-05013, and another reports one continuous interval of increase straight through a vertical asymptote.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A chart with the right partition points and a wrong sign on a piece is BC-SKL-05014 unfinished rather than a charting failure, while an inability to say where f is undefined for a piecewise, rational or radical form is BC-PRQ-05003, visible as a chart with no gap marked at all.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05012 (behaviour cannot be claimed across an input where the function does not exist) for the conceptual failure. Where the domain is understood and the signs themselves are wrong, the target is BC-SKL-05014.

skills.description_formal: Partition the domain at the critical points and the points of discontinuity, then record the sign of f' on each open piece.
skills.description_plain: Lay the critical points and gaps on a line and mark the sign in each gap.
skills.name: Build a sign chart on critical points and domain boundaries

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05013 (restating the conclusion is treated as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05008 (intervals of increase or decrease that must be supported by the sign of the named derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: The written reason names f prime as the object whose sign is being read and names f as the object that rises or falls, so a sentence such as f is increasing on that interval because f prime is positive there stands on its own without the reader having to guess the subject. The naming holds when the derivative is supplied as a plotted graph under BC-REP-04 as well as when it is supplied by formula, and neither BC-ERR-05018 (a reason whose subject is only the function or the graph) nor BC-ERR-99001 (it, the slope or the graph left as an unnamed subject) appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Intervals come out right and the supporting sentence still says the function or the graph rather than f prime, which is BC-SIG-05014 and matches BC-ERR-05018. A second intermediate state shows in the BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-C and BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-B scoring, where intervals earn their point while the reason is phrased about the function rather than the plotted derivative, or about the accumulation function rather than the integrand, so the reason point falls on a referent failure alone. In BC-FRQ-2013-Q1-C the comparison with the processing rate is made and the conclusion sentence is never written, which is the same gap in communication rather than in analysis.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the intervals themselves are wrong, the failure sits at BC-SKL-05016 (building a sign chart on critical points and domain boundaries) and not at the wording. The tell is that the sentence names f prime correctly and confidently while the interval endpoints do not match the zeros and undefined points of f prime, so naming is intact and the sign analysis under it is not.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05013 (a second sentence saying the conclusion again is taken for a justification) carries the conceptual failure. A procedural failure, where the student knows a name is required and writes the interval work without ever labelling which curve was plotted, points instead to BC-SKL-05016 (the sign chart, where the names are assigned).

skills.description_formal: State that f increases on an interval because f' is positive there, naming f explicitly rather than referring to the function or the graph.
skills.description_plain: Write the reason in words, naming the function whose derivative has that sign.
skills.name: Justify increase or decrease from the sign of the named derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05012 (a gap in the domain is taken not to interrupt an interval of behaviour)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05008 (intervals of increase or decrease that must be supported by the sign of the named derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any interval is written, the domain of f is settled, and the reported intervals of increase break at every input where f has no value, so two rising stretches on either side of a gap are reported as two intervals and never joined. This holds for a formula under BC-REP-01 and for a plotted derivative under BC-REP-04, and BC-ERR-05019 (one interval of increase reported straight across a gap in the domain) is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sign work is sound on each piece and the two correct stretches are merged into a single interval that spans the gap, which is BC-SIG-05015 and the observable form of BC-ERR-05019. Under BC-QA-05008 the interval half of the response fails on this alone while the sign reasoning that supports it is intact, and the reason point falls with the interval rather than on its own merits.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A student who cannot say where f is defined is failing at BC-PRQ-05003 (domain of a function, including piecewise, rational and radical forms) rather than at monotonicity. The sign of f prime is also read correctly piece by piece only when BC-SKL-05016 is in place, so a sign chart that omits the domain boundaries as break points points there instead.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-05003 (the domain as the set every conclusion about behaviour is restricted to) is the conceptual target. Where the domain is stated correctly and the break is still not drawn into the chart, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05016 (placing domain boundaries alongside critical points on the sign chart).

skills.description_formal: Report intervals of increase or decrease as subsets of the domain of f, splitting at any input where f is undefined.
skills.description_plain: Do not claim behaviour across a gap in the domain.
skills.name: Restrict a monotonicity conclusion to the domain of the function

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05008 (every critical point is taken to be an extremum)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every input offered as a possible relative extremum is a critical point, with the equation f prime of x equals zero written out and the inputs where f prime fails to exist carried across as well, and the list is defended by the statement that a relative extremum can occur only at a critical point. Nothing outside that list is tested, so BC-ERR-05020 (inputs that are neither critical points nor endpoints hunted over) does not appear, and the same list is produced whether f is given by formula under BC-REP-01 or read from a table or graph under BC-REP-02.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Correct critical inputs are listed with no equation behind them, which is BC-SIG-05007. BC-FRQ-2021-Q3-B records the same shape, a critical input asserted without the equation that produced it, and the setting of the supplied derivative equal to zero is exactly what the first point pays for. A further intermediate state is the candidate list treated as a finished answer, with each listed input assumed to be an extremum and no sign change checked.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An incomplete or wrong list traces back to BC-SKL-05010 (critical points where f prime equals zero) when the algebra of the equation is what breaks, or to BC-SKL-05011 (critical points where f prime fails to exist) when only the zeros appear and a corner or a vertical tangent is silently dropped. The tell for the second is a list that is correct on smooth pieces and empty exactly where the derivative is undefined.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05008 (a zero derivative read as the definition of a turning point) is where the conceptual repair sits. When the principle is stated correctly and the list is still short or padded, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05010 together with BC-SKL-05011 (producing the zeros and the undefined points of f prime).

skills.description_formal: From the critical points of f, form the list of candidate locations for relative extrema, citing that all relative extrema occur at critical points.
skills.description_plain: List the critical points as the only places a relative extremum can sit.
skills.name: Assemble the candidate relative extrema at the critical points

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05014 (the classification read off the value of the derivative rather than its change)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: At a critical point c the sign of f prime immediately to the left and immediately to the right is stated, and the classification follows the direction of the change, negative to positive giving a relative minimum and positive to negative giving a relative maximum. The reason cites the change of sign rather than how large f prime is nearby, so BC-ERR-05022 (classification taken from the value of the derivative instead of its change) is absent, and the direction is not inverted, so BC-ERR-05021 is absent. The same reading holds from a formula, from a table and from a plotted derivative, that is BC-REP-01, BC-REP-02 and BC-REP-03 alike.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sign change is described accurately and the verdict names the opposite extremum, which is BC-SIG-05016 and BC-ERR-05021. BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-A and BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-B both record the sign change read in the wrong direction, and BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-B additionally records the second derivative test attempted and miscomputed where the given information did not support it cheaply, and a verdict written with no reference to the sign of the derivative at all. BC-FRQ-2023-Q4-A records a correct conclusion reached through positive before and after phrasing, which does not state the sign-change criterion.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the signs on either side are themselves wrong, the break is at BC-SKL-05016 (the sign chart built on critical points and domain boundaries), and the tell is a correctly stated first derivative test applied to sign information that does not match f prime. If inputs are classified that were never critical points, the break is at BC-SKL-05019 (assembling the candidates at the critical points). Where the function under examination is an accumulation function, the relevant earlier skill is BC-SKL-06023 (locating relative extrema of an accumulation function from sign changes of the integrand), and the tell is sign work done on the accumulation curve rather than on the integrand.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05014 (size or single-sided sign of f prime taken as the classification) is the conceptual target. A procedural failure, where the criterion is stated correctly and the left and right signs are read off the wrong side, points instead to BC-SKL-05016 (the sign chart).

skills.description_formal: Determine the sign of f' immediately to the left and to the right of a critical point and classify the point as a relative maximum or a relative minimum accordingly.
skills.description_plain: Decide maximum or minimum from how the derivative sign flips there.
skills.name: Classify a critical point from the sign change of the first derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05008 (every critical point is taken to be an extremum)
BC-MIS-05014 (the classification read off the value of the derivative rather than its change)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: Where f prime is zero at c and holds one sign on both sides, the verdict is neither, and the sentence says that f prime does not change sign at c, which is the phrasing BC-FRQ-2023-Q4-A treats as sufficient on its own. Saying instead that f prime is positive before and after is not offered as the reason, so BC-ERR-05023 stays away, and no extremum is declared at such a point, so BC-ERR-05013 stays away. Any interval of positivity that is volunteered is correct, endpoints optional, and the conclusion reads the same from a formula under BC-REP-01 as from tabulated or graphical derivative information under BC-REP-02.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A relative maximum or minimum is announced at an input where f prime keeps its sign, which is BC-SIG-05010 and BC-ERR-05013, and BC-FRQ-2023-Q4-A records exactly that as a relative minimum claimed from a zero of the derivative. Closer in is the conclusion of neither reached correctly and supported by positive before and after, which is BC-ERR-05023 and costs the point although the verdict is right. BC-FRQ-2015-Q4-C shows a neighbouring state, the second derivative reached for where the first derivative was not zero, and a derivative evaluated with the conclusion sentence never written.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A student who cannot produce the signs on each side of c has not secured BC-SKL-05020 (classifying a critical point from the sign change of f prime), and the tell is that the neither case is refused not because the criterion is misunderstood but because no left and right signs were ever obtained.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05008 (f prime equal to zero taken as the definition of a turning point) is the conceptual target. When the verdict of neither is correct and only the wording fails, the target is BC-SKL-05020, where the sign-change criterion is phrased.

skills.description_formal: When f' has the same sign on both sides of a critical point, conclude that f has neither a relative maximum nor a relative minimum there.
skills.description_plain: Say neither when the derivative does not flip sign at the point.
skills.name: Conclude neither extremum when the derivative keeps its sign

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05013 (restating the conclusion is treated as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: One sentence carries three named things, f prime as the object changing sign, the direction of that change, and the input where it happens, so a reader meets no pronoun that has to be resolved. Nothing in the sentence is a restatement of the verdict in other symbols, and the naming survives when the derivative arrives only as a plotted curve under BC-REP-04, so neither BC-ERR-05018 (the function or the graph offered as the subject) nor BC-ERR-99001 (it or the slope left unnamed) is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The analysis is right and the sentence says the function or the graph rather than f prime, which is BC-SIG-05014 and BC-ERR-05018. The scoring records neighbouring states, BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-A losing the single answer-with-reason point for a correct input with no sign-change reason, BC-FRQ-2015-Q4-C recording a derivative evaluated and the conclusion left unwritten, BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-B recording a verdict with no reference to the sign of the derivative, and BC-FRQ-2023-Q4-A recording a reason given about the function rather than about its derivative.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the direction of the sign change written into the sentence is wrong, the writing is not at fault and BC-SKL-05020 (classifying a critical point from the sign change of the first derivative) is. The tell is a fully named, well-formed sentence that asserts a relative maximum for a change from negative to positive.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05013 (a restatement of the claim mistaken for evidence) is the conceptual target. Where the student knows a feature of the given information must be cited and still writes it or the graph out of habit, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05020, whose sign-change statement supplies the names.

skills.description_formal: Produce a sentence that names f', states the direction of its sign change, and names the input, avoiding an unnamed referent such as it or the graph.
skills.description_plain: Write the reason naming which derivative changes sign and where.
skills.name: Write a first derivative test justification with an explicit referent

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05015 (the location of an extremum and its value treated as the same answer)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
BC-QA-05006 (an absolute extremum found by the candidates test and justified over the whole interval)
adaptive.mastered_if: The question is read for which of two things it wants, the input c at which the extremum occurs or the extreme value f of c, and the reported answer is that one. Both are available in the work, so when the value is asked for the function is evaluated at c rather than c being handed back, and BC-ERR-05024 (location reported where the value was wanted, or the reverse) does not occur. This holds for a formula under BC-REP-01 and for a justification written in words under BC-REP-04.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The extremum is located correctly and the reported answer is the input where the value was demanded, or the value where the input was demanded, which is BC-SIG-05017 and BC-ERR-05024. BC-FRQ-2021-Q3-B records two related states, a critical input found with the curve never evaluated there so the link from the maximum to the radius is missing, and the derivative value handed in as the radius, which confuses a function value with a derivative value rather than a location with a value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the point was never classified, there is nothing to report either way and the failure belongs to BC-SKL-05020 (classifying a critical point from the sign change of the first derivative). The tell is that the answer is unstable between candidate inputs rather than between an input and its output.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05015 (input and output collapsed into one answer) is the conceptual target. When the distinction is held and the wrong one is still submitted because the question was scanned rather than read, the target is BC-SKL-05020, where the classified point and its value are both on the page.

skills.description_formal: Given a classified critical point, report the input where the extremum occurs or the value f(c), according to the wording of the question.
skills.description_plain: Answer with the input or the output, whichever was asked for.
skills.name: Separate the location of a relative extremum from its value

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05016 (the candidates taken to be the critical points only)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (an absolute extremum found by the candidates test and justified over the whole interval)
adaptive.mastered_if: For f continuous on the closed interval from a to b, the candidate list holds every critical point lying strictly inside, together with a and b, and nothing else. Critical points found outside the interval are named and discarded rather than carried forward, so BC-ERR-05025 is absent, and both ends are evaluated rather than assumed to lose, so BC-ERR-05026 is absent. The equation f prime of x equals zero is written and considered, which BC-QA-05006 pays for separately from merely listing zeros, and the open versus closed distinction is respected in how the interval is written, whether f arrives as a formula under BC-REP-01 or as a table or graph under BC-REP-02.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: All interior critical points are present and one or both endpoints are missing from the comparison, which is BC-SIG-05018 and BC-ERR-05026, and BC-FRQ-2019-Q1-C records endpoints omitted from a candidates table directly. BC-FRQ-2013-Q1-D records a candidates table without the endpoints described as a local argument offered where a global one was demanded, and BC-FRQ-2019-Q3-C records a critical point found with only a local sign change cited. BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-B shows the list assembled correctly with the candidate values computed wrongly from the areas, which is an accumulation failure sitting on top of a sound candidate list, and its rubric makes the justification point unavailable once the answer is wrong.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An empty or partial list of interior candidates comes from BC-SKL-05010 (critical points where f prime equals zero) or BC-SKL-05011 (critical points where f prime fails to exist), the tell being a list correct on smooth pieces and silent where the derivative is undefined. When the endpoints are known to matter and the interval is written with the wrong kind of endpoint, or an interior point is taken for an end, the gap is BC-PRQ-05004 (interval notation and the open versus closed distinction).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05016 (the ends of the interval not regarded as competitors) is the conceptual target. A procedural failure, where the endpoints are named as candidates and then never evaluated or an outside critical point is dragged into the comparison, points instead to BC-PRQ-05004 (reading the interval and its ends as written).

skills.description_formal: Given f continuous on [a,b], collect the critical points in (a,b) together with a and b as the complete candidate list for the absolute extrema.
skills.description_plain: Write down every critical point in the interval plus the two endpoints.
skills.name: Assemble the candidate list from critical points and both endpoints

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05016 (the candidates are the critical points only, so endpoints never compete)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every entry of the candidate table carries a computed value of f, whether the value comes from substituting into a formula, reading a given table, or accumulating signed area under a plotted f prime, and the endpoint entries are evaluated with the same care as the interior critical inputs. Values agree with the supplied information, areas under the axis are subtracted rather than added, and BC-ERR-05027, a wrong value at one candidate, does not appear anywhere in the table.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The candidate list is complete and one evaluated entry contradicts the given information, which is BC-SIG-05019. The failure sits in BC-ERR-05027, a single mis-evaluated candidate, and it strips the justification point outright under the 2023 guideline even though the rest of the table stands. The 2013 Q4 commentary describes the same shape, with candidates correctly listed and their values computed wrongly from the plotted areas.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the list being evaluated has no endpoint entries in it at all, the break is upstream in BC-SKL-05024, assembling the candidate list from critical points and both endpoints, rather than in the evaluation. A second upstream tell is BC-PRQ-06005, where f(t) and f prime of t are not held apart, so the response evaluates the rate function at the candidate instead of the accumulated amount.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06005 (function notation and evaluation at a stated input) carries the conceptual failure, where a function is not distinguished from its value. Procedural failure, meaning the table is right in form and one number is wrong, points instead to BC-SKL-05024 and to the area bookkeeping behind BC-ERR-05027.

skills.description_formal: Compute f at each entry of the candidate list, from a formula, from a table, or by accumulating area under a plotted derivative.
skills.description_plain: Work out the function value at each candidate input.
skills.name: Evaluate the function at every candidate

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05017 (the last candidate computed is taken to be the extremum)
BC-MIS-05016 (the candidates are the critical points only, so endpoints never compete)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: Ordering happens explicitly. The tabulated candidate values are compared against one another, the largest is named when a maximum is asked for and the smallest when a minimum is asked for, and the selected candidate is stated with its value rather than left implicit in the last line of arithmetic. BC-ERR-05028, choosing the extremum in the wrong direction, is absent, and the comparison covers every row of the table including both endpoint rows.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct candidate table followed by the wrong selection, recorded as BC-SIG-05020, is the intermediate state here. BC-ERR-05028 costs the answer point while leaving the table itself intact. The 2022 Q1 commentary notes a related partial shape, where the value is correct but no candidates are listed, so the justification requirement goes unmet even though the selection was sound.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the numbers being ordered are themselves wrong, nothing in the comparison is at fault and the gap belongs to BC-SKL-05025, evaluating the function at every candidate. The tell is a table whose ordering is internally consistent while one entry disagrees with the given rate information or the plotted area.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05017 (the comparison is never carried out and the last line becomes the answer) is the conceptual target. Where the comparison is attempted and the direction is simply inverted, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05025, since the ordering rests on the evaluated values.

skills.description_formal: Order the computed values and identify which candidate gives the absolute maximum and which the absolute minimum on the interval.
skills.description_plain: Pick the largest or smallest of the candidate values.
skills.name: Compare the candidate values and name the absolute extremum

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05015 (the location of an extremum and its value treated as the same answer)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response answers the question that was posed. A request for the absolute minimum value returns a number produced by f, and a request for where the minimum occurs returns the input, with the two written distinctly rather than folded into one statement. The 2023 guideline awarded the answer point only for the minimum value and not for the input, and a mastered response respects that split, so BC-ERR-05024 does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Correct location, wrong reported object. BC-SIG-05017 describes work that finds the extremum accurately and then reports the input where the value was wanted, or the value where the input was wanted. BC-ERR-05024 is the named failure, and it costs the answer point on its own, which the 2013 Q4 and 2022 Q3 commentaries both record as a location-versus-value confusion.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An answer that names the wrong candidate entirely, not merely the wrong object, sits in BC-SKL-05026, comparing the candidate values and naming the absolute extremum. The sign of that earlier gap is a reported input that does not correspond to the extreme row of the candidate table.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05015 (input and extreme value collapsed into one object) is the conceptual target. When both quantities are held apart in the work and the transcription to the final line picks the wrong one, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05026, where the selected candidate and its value are paired.

skills.description_formal: Distinguish a question asking for the absolute minimum value from one asking for the input at which it occurs, and answer the one posed.
skills.description_plain: Give the value asked for, not just where it happens.
skills.name: Report the extreme value rather than only its location

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05018 (a local test treated as settling a global question)
BC-MIS-05017 (the last candidate computed is taken to be the extremum)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: An argument covering the whole interval appears, not a sign change at one input. Evaluations or equivalent reasoning are shown for each candidate, both endpoints are among them, no extra inputs are declared, and a comparison sentence names which candidate beats the rest. The 2023 guideline withholds the justification point from any response that fails to consider both endpoints, and the 2025 exactness rule withholds it for surplus candidates, so BC-ERR-05026 and BC-ERR-99004 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Two intermediate states show up. In BC-SIG-05021 the answer is right and the justification is a first or second derivative test at the candidate, which is BC-ERR-05029 and BC-ERR-99004, a local argument standing in for a global one. In the other, the comparison runs but the ends of the interval are never evaluated, which is BC-ERR-05026. Each leaves the answer point available and removes the justification point.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A justification that quotes candidate values disagreeing with the given information fails upstream in BC-SKL-05025, evaluating the function at every candidate, and the tell is a well formed comparison built on a bad number. Where the comparison itself picks the wrong direction, the gap is BC-SKL-05026 instead.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05018 (a first or second derivative test believed to prove a claim about the whole interval) is the conceptual target. A response that accepts the global requirement but omits an endpoint row is procedural and points to BC-SKL-05024, assembling the candidate list from critical points and both endpoints.

skills.description_formal: Present evaluations or reasoning for each candidate, including both endpoints and no additional inputs, and state the comparison that selects the extremum.
skills.description_plain: Show the comparison over all candidates, endpoints included, and nothing else.
skills.name: Write a global justification covering every candidate

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05018 (a local test treated as settling a global question)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: The derivative argument is stated across the interval rather than at a point. Work shows f prime not positive on one side of the candidate and not negative on the other, over the full stretch to each end of the interval, and the conclusion names the absolute extremum that this sign behaviour forces. The 2025 and 2026 guidelines accept either a sign discussion or a candidates comparison for the justification point, and this route is carried far enough that BC-ERR-05029 and BC-ERR-99004 do not apply.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05021 captures the recurring middle state, a correct extremum paired with a first or second derivative test at the candidate. BC-ERR-05029 names that substitution of a local test for a global one, and BC-ERR-99004 widens it to include a sign change cited at a single point. The 2019 Q1 and 2021 Q2 commentaries both record critical inputs located correctly and justified only locally.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the sign of f prime is assigned wrongly on a stretch, the break is in BC-SKL-05016, building a sign chart on critical points and domain boundaries, and the tell is a partition whose intervals are right while one carries the wrong sign. A response that never identifies the relevant candidate at all sits in BC-SKL-05024 instead.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05018 (local sign change mistaken for proof over the whole interval) is the conceptual target. When the global intent is present and the sign chart underneath it is faulty, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05016, where the signs of f prime on each interval are established.

skills.description_formal: Show f' not positive on one side of the candidate and not negative on the other across the whole interval, and conclude the absolute extremum there.
skills.description_plain: Argue globally from the derivative keeping one sign on each side.
skills.name: Justify an absolute extremum from the sign of the derivative across the interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05019 (rules about the first derivative transferred onto the second without re-deriving them)
BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05004 (intervals of concavity from derivative information with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: Concavity is reported from f double prime and nothing else. The second derivative is computed, its zeros and undefined inputs partition the domain, the sign of f double prime on each open interval is determined from a test value or a factored form, and concave up is claimed exactly where that sign is positive. In implicit settings the first derivative is substituted back so no derivative symbol survives in f double prime, and BC-ERR-05030, a misread sign on one interval, is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05022 gives the shape to watch for, a correct partition with one interval labelled with the wrong concavity, which is BC-ERR-05030. Because the 2023 rubric makes the reason point available only after the interval point is earned, this single sign error removes both. The 2015 Q4 commentary adds a nearby partial state, a sign asserted without naming the variable signs that produce it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Zeros or undefined inputs of f double prime that are wrong or incomplete place the gap in BC-PRQ-05001, solving equations and inequalities to locate where an expression is zero or undefined. When the partition is right and the sign on each piece is guessed rather than tested, the gap is BC-PRQ-05002, sign analysis of a factored expression across a number line.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05019 (the second derivative assumed to say about f what the first says) is the conceptual target, since it produces intervals of increase in place of intervals of concavity. Procedural failure, where the referent is right and one sign is wrong, points to BC-PRQ-05002.

skills.description_formal: Compute f'', find its zeros and undefined points, and determine the sign of f'' on each resulting open interval to report concavity.
skills.description_plain: Use where the second derivative is positive or negative.
skills.name: Determine intervals of concavity from the sign of the second derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve taken to be the function under discussion)
BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05004 (intervals of concavity from derivative information with a reason)
BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives)
adaptive.mastered_if: Rising and falling of the plotted f prime drive the answer, not whether that plot sits above or below the axis. Intervals on which the drawn derivative climbs are reported as concave up for the graph of f, the stated reason names the derivative increasing or decreasing rather than the function, the two curves are labelled separately, and the reported intervals stay inside the stated domain. BC-ERR-05031 and BC-ERR-05016, both forms of confusing increase with positivity, do not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05023 marks the not-mastered end, where the reported intervals are exactly the stretches on which the plotted derivative lies above the axis, which is BC-ERR-05031 and its wider relative BC-ERR-05016. A milder state appears in the 2014 Q3 and 2013 Q4 commentaries, correct intervals paired with a reason phrased about the accumulation function instead of the plotted derivative, which loses the reason point alone.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A response that cannot say where the drawn curve rises or falls, independently of any calculus claim, is short on BC-PRQ-05006, reading features of a graph including where it rises, falls, and changes bending. The tell is inconsistent reading of the picture itself, with turning points of the plot placed where the plot crosses the axis.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05020 (rising and bending upward not separated) is the conceptual target, with BC-MIS-05011 alongside it when the drawn curve is answered about directly. Procedural failure, meaning correct intervals with the reason attached to the wrong curve, points to BC-SKL-01059 and the habit of naming the referent before reading a feature off a plot.

skills.description_formal: From a plotted f', identify the intervals where the plot is increasing and where it is decreasing, and report the graph of f as concave up or concave down there.
skills.description_plain: Read concavity off the slope behaviour of the derivative graph.
skills.name: Determine concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05021 (a zero of the second derivative taken to be a point of inflection with no sign change checked)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05005 (points of inflection identified with a reason tied to the given graph)
adaptive.mastered_if: Solving f double prime equal to zero is followed by a domain filter. Inputs where f double prime fails to exist are collected too, anything lying outside the domain of f is discarded, and the surviving list is offered as candidates rather than as a finished set of inflection points, leaving the sign change still to be checked. The 2025 and 2026 guidelines award the answer point only for the exact set, so no surplus input appears and BC-ERR-05032 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: An input where f has no value sits in the declared list, which is BC-SIG-05024 and BC-ERR-05032, and the extra entry costs the answer point on its own. The 2025 Q4 commentary describes a second partial state, two of three required inputs given because a turning point between pieces was missed, and the 2026 Q4 note records the reverse cost, where declaring a point instead of an input value forfeits eligibility for the reason.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Missing or spurious zeros of f double prime come from BC-PRQ-05001, solving equations and inequalities to locate where an expression is zero or undefined, and show up as a candidate list that does not match the second derivative written just above it. When the algebra is right and the undefined inputs are kept anyway, the gap is BC-PRQ-05003, the domain of a function in piecewise, rational, and radical forms.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05021 (candidate condition equated with the conclusion) is the conceptual target. Where the candidate status is understood and an out-of-domain input still survives, the procedural target is BC-PRQ-05003, restricting every conclusion to the set of inputs on which f is defined.

skills.description_formal: Solve f'' equal to zero and find where f'' fails to exist, retaining only inputs that lie in the domain of f.
skills.description_plain: Find the inputs where the second derivative is zero or does not exist.
skills.name: Locate candidate points of inflection where the second derivative is zero or undefined

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05021 (a zero of the second derivative treated as a point of inflection)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05005 (points of inflection identified with a reason tied to the given graph)
adaptive.mastered_if: A candidate input is only called a point of inflection after the learner writes what the second derivative does on the left and on the right, or equivalently that f prime turns from decreasing to increasing there, and the declared list contains exactly the inputs where that reversal happens. Work on a plotted derivative and work on a formula both produce the same list, and neither BC-ERR-05033 (every zero of the second derivative reported as an inflection point) nor BC-ERR-99023 (inflection points misidentified or justified without the given representation) appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The inputs come out right but the sign change is never written down, which is the BC-SIG-05025 observation of a list that matches the zeros exactly with no sign discussion, so BC-ERR-05033 stands. Another intermediate state is a correct set of inputs carried by a reason phrased purely in second derivative symbols, the split named in the 2025 guidelines where the answer point survives and the reason point does not, close to BC-ERR-99023.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Zeros of the plotted function are offered as the candidates, which is a failure of BC-SKL-05032 (locating candidates where the second derivative is zero or undefined) rather than of the sign check, and the tell is that the reported inputs are extrema or axis crossings of the given curve. A reversed reading of concavity from a rising or falling derivative graph points instead to BC-SKL-05031.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05021 (candidate condition equated with the conclusion) for the conceptual failure. When the concept is held but the two sided check is skipped or botched, the target is BC-SKL-05032 (producing the candidate list correctly before testing it).

skills.description_formal: Show that f'' takes opposite signs on the two sides of a candidate input, equivalently that f' changes from decreasing to increasing or the reverse, before declaring a point of inflection.
skills.description_plain: Check the bending really changes direction there.
skills.name: Confirm a point of inflection by a sign change of the second derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05021 (a zero of the second derivative treated as a point of inflection)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05005 (points of inflection identified with a reason tied to the given graph)
adaptive.mastered_if: An input where the second derivative touches zero and returns to the same sign is named and then excluded, with the shared sign on both sides stated rather than assumed. The final list carries no extra entry, which is what protects the answer point under the BC-QA-05005 rule that any extra input inside the interval forfeits it, and BC-ERR-05034 (touching zero kept as a point of inflection) is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Two of three declared inputs are correct while a touching zero remains in the list, exactly the BC-SIG-05026 observation, so BC-ERR-05034 is live and the answer point is gone even though most of the work is sound. A related state keeps the extra entry and also leans on second derivative language alone for the reason, which brings in BC-ERR-99023 (inflection claims not tied to the given representation).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If no sign comparison is being made anywhere, not only at the disputed input, the break is at BC-SKL-05033 (confirming an inflection point by a sign change) and the tell is a list that reproduces the zeros of the second derivative wholesale.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05021 (the candidate condition read as sufficient) for the conceptual case; when the rule is stated correctly but the touching zero still survives the filter, the target is BC-SKL-05033 (carrying out the two sided sign comparison).

skills.description_formal: When f'' is zero at an input but keeps the same sign on both sides, exclude that input from the list of points of inflection.
skills.description_plain: Throw out a candidate where the bending does not change.
skills.name: Reject a candidate where the second derivative is zero without a sign change

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05013 (restating the conclusion counted as a reason)
BC-MIS-05022 (a reason treated as complete once derivative symbols appear)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05005 (points of inflection identified with a reason tied to the given graph)
BC-QA-05004 (intervals of concavity from derivative information with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: The reason names the object the question supplied, for instance that the plotted f changes from decreasing to increasing at that input, or that the plotted derivative is positive and decreasing across the interval, instead of asserting a sign change of f double prime.
