Every subject is named rather than left as it or the graph, so BC-ERR-99001 (vague referent in a justification) is absent, and the phrasing survives both the inflection archetype BC-QA-05005 and the concavity interval archetype BC-QA-05004.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Inputs or intervals are exactly right while the reason cites a sign change of the second derivative, the BC-SIG-05027 observation and BC-ERR-05035, which loses the reason point and leaves the answer point standing. A second state names a subject but the wrong one, such as a reason phrased about the accumulation function when the plotted derivative was given, recorded in BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-B and BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-C as a referent failure, and an unnamed subject falls under BC-ERR-99001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the listed inputs themselves are wrong, the reason wording is not the binding constraint and the gap sits at BC-SKL-05033 (confirming an inflection point by a sign change). The tell is that the correction to the phrasing would still leave the list unearned, and under BC-QA-05004 the reason point is not even available while the intervals are wrong.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05013 (a restated conclusion mistaken for a justification) when the failure is conceptual, and BC-MIS-05022 (symbols standing in for a statement about the given object) when the learner can say what the given plot does but still writes the sentence in derivative notation.

skills.description_formal: Phrase the reason using the named given function, for example that the plotted f changes from decreasing to increasing, rather than restating the conclusion in second derivative symbols or using an unnamed referent.
skills.description_plain: Write the reason in terms of the object the question actually supplied.
skills.name: Tie a concavity or inflection reason to the representation that was given

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05023 (the second derivative test treated as always decisive)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05013 (second derivative test applied at a critical point)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any second derivative is evaluated, the learner records that f prime is zero at the input, then reports f double prime there and reads a negative value as a relative maximum and a positive value as a relative minimum. The direction of the correspondence holds under rewording and the classification is never applied at a non critical input, so BC-ERR-05036 (test used where the first derivative is not zero) and BC-ERR-05037 (sign convention reversed) both stay out.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Arithmetic on f double prime is correct and the extremum type comes out the opposite way, the BC-SIG-05028 observation and BC-ERR-05037. Another state evaluates the second derivative at an input never shown to be critical and classifies from it, which is BC-ERR-05036 and costs the justification point. A third pattern, visible in BC-FRQ-2026-Q2-C, classifies from the sign of the radial function rather than from the derivative.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the inputs fed into the test are not critical points at all, the earlier failure is BC-SKL-05010 (finding critical points where the first derivative equals zero), and the tell is a second derivative evaluated at a convenient input with no zero of f prime written anywhere. A learner who cannot say which way a curve bends for a negative second derivative is short of BC-SKL-05030.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05023 (no room held for the inconclusive case) for the conceptual failure. A reversed verdict with sound mechanics points instead to BC-SKL-05030 (reading concavity from the sign of the second derivative), since the sign to shape link is what has slipped.

skills.description_formal: At an input where f' is zero, evaluate f'' and classify the point as a relative maximum when f'' is negative and a relative minimum when f'' is positive.
skills.description_plain: Use the sign of the second derivative at the point to classify it.
skills.name: Apply the second derivative test at a critical point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05023 (the second derivative test treated as always decisive)
BC-MIS-05024 (the two derivative tests treated as interchangeable everywhere)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05013 (second derivative test applied at a critical point)
adaptive.mastered_if: Where f double prime of c is zero at a critical point, the response says in words that the second derivative test settles nothing there and then turns to the sign of f prime on either side of c to classify. The switch is made explicitly rather than by silently abandoning the first attempt, and BC-ERR-05038 (a vanishing second derivative read as the verdict neither maximum nor minimum) does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The zero second derivative is treated as a finding and the point is declared neither a maximum nor a minimum, which is BC-SIG-05029 and BC-ERR-05038, leaving the classification unsupported. A softer state names the case as inconclusive and then stops, with no first derivative sign argument supplied, so the classification demanded by BC-QA-05013 is never delivered.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A learner who cannot apply the test in the ordinary non zero case is short of BC-SKL-05036 (applying the second derivative test at a critical point), and the tell is that the negative and positive verdicts are themselves unstable or reversed, with the zero case only one more variant of that instability.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05023 (a zero second derivative mistaken for a verdict) for the conceptual failure. When the inconclusive case is named correctly but no replacement argument follows, the target is BC-SKL-05036, since the test mechanics themselves are not yet reliable enough to hand off from.

skills.description_formal: When f''(c) equals zero at a critical point, declare the second derivative test inconclusive and apply the first derivative test instead.
skills.description_plain: Say that a zero second derivative settles nothing and switch tests.
skills.name: State the inconclusive case of the second derivative test

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05018 (a local test taken to settle a global question)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
BC-QA-05013 (second derivative test applied at a critical point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The step from local to global is written out. The response states that the interval holds exactly one critical point, that f is continuous there, and that the relative extremum found at that input is therefore the absolute extremum on the interval. The uniqueness clause is present in words, not implied by the layout of the work, so BC-ERR-05039 (sole critical point claim made without stating uniqueness) and BC-ERR-99004 (a local argument offered where a global one is required) are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct relative classification is promoted to an absolute claim with the uniqueness sentence missing, matching BC-SIG-05030 and BC-ERR-05039, so the justification is incomplete at exactly the joint that makes it global. Related states run a candidates test that skips an endpoint or an interior critical point, or rest the global claim on a single sign change, both covered by BC-ERR-99004, and under BC-QA-05011 a verification that argues only locally does not earn the verification point.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the relative classification itself is shaky, the earlier failure is BC-SKL-05020 (classifying a critical point from the sign change of the first derivative) or BC-SKL-05036 (the second derivative test), and the tell is that the extremum type is wrong before any question of the whole interval arises.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05018 (local evidence treated as proof about the whole interval) for the conceptual failure. When the learner knows a global claim needs more but leaves out the sentence, the target is BC-SKL-05020, where the sign change argument and the count of critical points on the interval are assembled.

skills.description_formal: Given f continuous on an interval with exactly one critical point that is a relative extremum, conclude that it is the absolute extremum on that interval, stating the uniqueness.
skills.description_plain: When there is only one critical point, a relative extremum there is the extreme value overall.
skills.name: Extend a sole relative extremum to an absolute extremum on the interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05024 (the two derivative tests treated as interchangeable everywhere)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05013 (second derivative test applied at a critical point)
BC-QA-05007 (critical point located and classified for a function given indirectly)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given a plotted f prime, a formula, or a differential equation, the learner names which derivative the object actually shows and picks the test that information supports, so a graph of the first derivative draws a sign change argument while a differentiable formula or a relation that can be differentiated again admits the second derivative test, and the choice is stated with its reason rather than left implicit. BC-ERR-05040 (a test chosen that the given information cannot support) does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A second derivative test is started from a graph of the first derivative with nothing said about the slope of that graph, the BC-SIG-05031 observation and BC-ERR-05040, so the argument cannot be finished from what was given. BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-B records the neighbouring state where a second derivative test is attempted and miscomputed when the sign argument was cheaper, and BC-FRQ-2026-Q2-C records a candidates table presented where a derivative test was demanded.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When neither test can be executed cleanly once chosen, the gap is at BC-SKL-05020 (classifying from the sign change of the first derivative) or BC-SKL-05036 (applying the second derivative test), and the tell is that a defensible choice is followed by a broken execution rather than by an argument the given object cannot carry.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05024 (test picked by habit rather than by what the representation supports) for the conceptual failure, with BC-SKL-05036 as the procedural target when the second derivative test is chosen appropriately and then miscarried.

skills.description_formal: Given a function presented as a graph of f', a formula, or a differential equation, select the derivative test that the available information makes usable and say why.
skills.description_plain: Pick the test the given information actually supports.
skills.name: Choose between the first and second derivative tests for a given presentation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (whatever curve is drawn taken to be the function under discussion)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives)
adaptive.mastered_if: Zeros of the sketched f prime land at the turning points of the plotted f, the sketch sits above the axis where f rises and below it where f falls, and its steepness tracks how fast f climbs or drops. The two curves are kept apart in the labelling, so features of f are read off f and features of f prime off the sketch, and BC-ERR-05041 (turning points of the derivative sketch placed at the zeros of the function) is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The drawn derivative turns where the original curve crosses the axis, which is BC-SIG-05032 and BC-ERR-05041, a single misplacement that breaks every feature check downstream even when the general shape looks plausible. A milder state gets the sign of f prime right across each stretch while the relative steepness is flat and uninformative, so the size part of the slope record is missing.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the turning points, axis crossings and rising or falling stretches of the plotted f cannot be extracted in the first place, the failure is at BC-PRQ-05006 (reading features of a graph) rather than at the derivative relationship, and the tell is that the learner misreports features of the original curve before any sketching starts.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve conflated with the function being asked about) for the conceptual failure, while a learner who states the horizontal tangent rule correctly and still draws it wrong points to BC-PRQ-05006 (extracting extrema and crossings from the given plot).

skills.description_formal: From a plotted f, plot f' by recording the sign and the size of the slope, placing zeros of f' at the turning points of f.
skills.description_plain: Turn the slopes of a curve into a new plotted curve.
skills.name: Sketch the graph of the derivative from the graph of a function

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve is treated as the function under discussion)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: The drawn curve rises exactly on the stretches where the plotted f prime sits above the axis, falls where it sits below, and changes bending at the inputs where f prime turns, with every relative extremum of the sketch placed at a crossing of the axis by f prime rather than at a turning point of it. BC-ERR-05042, putting turning points of the sketch at the zeros of the wrong object, is absent, and so is BC-ERR-05016, reporting concavity when monotonicity was asked for or reading increase of f off a rising f prime.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Slopes and directions come out right on part of the domain while the bending information is read off the wrong feature, matching BC-SIG-05033, where the drawn function turns where the given derivative turns instead of where it crosses the axis. Another partial state keeps the shape roughly correct but swaps the two vocabularies, which is BC-ERR-05016, increase of the derivative confused with positivity of the derivative, so extrema and inflection points end up interchanged across the sketch in the way BC-ERR-05042 describes.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Reading the sign of f prime off the plot is itself unreliable, which is BC-SKL-05015, reading intervals of increase and decrease from the graph of the derivative. The tell is that the sketch rises and falls on stretches that do not line up with where the plotted curve is above or below the axis, so no amount of attention to bending repairs it. A second earlier failure is BC-SKL-05031, deciding concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls, shown by a sketch whose bends are unrelated to the slopes of f prime.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve read as the function itself) for the conceptual failure, while a sketch built on the right referent but drawn with features in the wrong places points instead to BC-SKL-05015 (reading intervals of increase and decrease off the derivative graph)

skills.description_formal: From a plotted f', draw a curve that rises where f' is positive, falls where f' is negative, and changes bending where f' turns.
skills.description_plain: Turn a derivative plot back into a curve with the right rises, falls, and bends.
skills.name: Sketch a possible graph of a function from the graph of its derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve is treated as the function under discussion)
BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given a named feature, the response pairs it with the correct object every time: a relative extremum of f with a sign change of f prime, a point of inflection of f with a sign change of f double prime, an interval of decrease of f with f prime negative there. The pairing survives moving between an analytic description, a plotted curve, and a table of values, and BC-ERR-05043, matching a feature of the function with the wrong derivative, never appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correspondences are internally consistent but every one is shifted by a single derivative in the same direction, which is BC-SIG-05034 and the pattern named in BC-ERR-05043, so a point of inflection gets paired with a zero of f prime and an extremum with a zero of f double prime. A weaker state mixes rising with being positive, the substance of BC-ERR-05043 when combined with confusing concavity and monotonicity. Scoring on BC-FRQ-2026-Q4-B shows the cost: listing zeros of the derivative when inflection was at issue, and writing an ordered pair instead of an input value, which earns the input point but forfeits eligibility for the reason.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The failure sits in BC-SKL-05031, determining concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls, when the response cannot say what f double prime does without first drawing something. The sign is that questions about intervals of decrease are answered correctly while any question naming bending is answered by slope, pointing back to BC-SKL-05015 for the monotonicity half.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05020 (rising and bending upward collapsed into one property) for the conceptual failure; a uniform one-derivative displacement with the concepts intact points instead to BC-SKL-05031 (concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls)

skills.description_formal: Given a feature such as a relative maximum, a point of inflection, or an interval of decrease, name the corresponding feature on the graph of f' or f''.
skills.description_plain: Say which feature of one graph corresponds to a feature of the other.
skills.name: Match a named feature of a function with the corresponding feature of its derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every relative extremum on the finished sketch sits at an input where f prime changes sign, and every point of inflection sits where f double prime changes sign, so no bending change coincides with a horizontal tangent unless the derivative information actually put one there. The sketch can be checked against the derivative data point by point without contradiction, and BC-ERR-05044, drawing a point of inflection at a turning point of the curve with no justification, does not occur.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Turning points land correctly while inflection points are attached to the same inputs, the situation BC-ERR-05044 describes, so the finished drawing contradicts the derivative data it was built from. BC-SIG-05033 covers the harsher case, where the drawn function turns where the given derivative turns rather than where it crosses the axis, leaving both families of features misplaced together.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The earlier break is BC-SKL-05041, sketching a possible graph of a function from the graph of its derivative, recognisable when the overall rise and fall pattern is already wrong before any feature is placed. When rise and fall are right but the second derivative sign change is never checked, the gap is BC-SKL-05033, confirming a point of inflection by a sign change of the second derivative.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05020 (slope and bending used interchangeably) for the conceptual failure, and BC-SKL-05033 (confirming a point of inflection by a sign change of the second derivative) when the idea is sound but the check is skipped

skills.description_formal: Position every relative extremum at a sign change of f' and every point of inflection at a sign change of f'' when drawing the curve.
skills.description_plain: Put the turning points and bending changes where the derivative information puts them.
skills.name: Place extrema and points of inflection consistently on a sketch

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05025 (a derivative believed to determine its function uniquely)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: A reconstruction from f prime is stated as determined only up to an additive constant, and a supplied value such as f at a given input is used to fix that constant before any specific claim about f is made. Shifting the drawn curve vertically is acknowledged as producing an equally valid answer when no value of f was given. BC-ERR-05045, asserting that one particular curve is the graph of the function when only the derivative was supplied, is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The shape is right and the ambiguity is never mentioned, which is BC-SIG-05035, asserting a unique graph of the function from derivative information alone. A nearer state names the constant but does not use the supplied value to pin it, leaving a claim stronger than the information supports in the sense of BC-ERR-05045.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the reconstructed shape itself is wrong, the ambiguity question never arises and the failure belongs to BC-SKL-05041, sketching a possible graph of a function from the graph of its derivative. The tell is a curve whose rises and falls do not track the sign of f prime, so the vertical placement is not what is at issue.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05025 (one derivative thought to fix one curve) for the conceptual failure; when the constant is named but never solved for from a given value, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05041 (building the curve from the derivative graph)

skills.description_formal: State that the graph of f reconstructed from f' is determined up to an additive constant, and use a supplied value of f to fix it.
skills.description_plain: Note that one known value is needed to pin the curve down.
skills.name: Recognise the vertical shift ambiguity when a curve is drawn from its derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve is treated as the function under discussion)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: Three unlabelled curves get the labels f, f prime, and f double prime by checking which curve has zeros at the turning points of which, and the direction of that relation runs the right way twice in a row. The assignment is defended by naming one concrete pairing, such as a relative maximum of the candidate for f sitting above a crossing of the axis by the candidate for f prime. BC-ERR-05046, ordering the three graphs in the reverse derivative direction, does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The labelling is internally consistent and runs backwards, so f is called the second derivative and the second derivative is called f, which is BC-SIG-05036 and exactly BC-ERR-05046. Every subsequent feature question is then answered about the wrong object even though the reasoning within the triple is sound.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The earlier failure is BC-SKL-05042, matching a named feature of a function with the corresponding feature of its derivative. The sign is that a single pairing cannot be stated correctly in isolation, so the three way sort has no rule to apply twice.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05011 (whatever curve is drawn read as the function) for the conceptual failure, with a consistent but reversed ordering pointing instead to BC-SKL-05042 (matching one named feature with the corresponding feature of the derivative)

skills.description_formal: Given three plotted curves, assign the labels f, f', and f'' by matching turning points of one with zeros and sign changes of another.
skills.description_plain: Sort three unlabelled curves into the right roles.
skills.name: Identify which of several graphs is the function, the derivative, and the second derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
BC-QA-05004 (intervals of concavity from derivative information, with the reason point available only when the intervals are correct)
adaptive.mastered_if: A claim that f double prime is positive on an interval is turned into concave up for the graph of f and increasing for f prime, and a claim that f double prime is decreasing is kept separate from a claim that it is negative. The statement is made for the whole interval rather than at a single input, and the sign is quoted rather than the direction. BC-ERR-05047, calling the graph concave up where the second derivative is decreasing, does not occur.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct reading of f double prime is converted into the opposite concavity claim, which is BC-SIG-05037, and any inflection list built afterwards inherits the error as BC-ERR-05047 notes. The scoring behaviour on BC-FRQ-2023-Q3-C shows a second intermediate state, where the second derivative is left in terms of the first and the substitution back into the differential equation is never carried out, and a third where concavity is argued only at the initial point. BC-FRQ-2026-Q3-C adds the case where concavity is attributed to the derivative rather than the function, and the case where concave up is claimed but an overestimate is asserted, inverting the relationship between bending and tangent line position.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When nothing can be said about f prime from f double prime without a picture, the gap is BC-SKL-05031, determining concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls. If the concavity statement is right and the consequence for a tangent line estimate is inverted, the earlier skill is BC-SKL-04030, deciding whether a tangent line approximation over or under estimates.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05020 (bending and rising treated as one property) for the conceptual failure, while a correct sign statement paired with the wrong estimate direction points to BC-SKL-04030 (whether a tangent line approximation over or under estimates)

skills.description_formal: Given the sign or the monotonicity of f'' on an interval, state the corresponding concavity of the graph of f and the monotonicity of f'.
skills.description_plain: Turn a claim about the second derivative into a claim about bending.
skills.name: Translate a statement about the second derivative into a statement about shape

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05012 (a gap in the domain not treated as interrupting an interval of behaviour)
BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: The number line is cut at the zeros and the undefined points of f prime and of f double prime, not anywhere else, and each resulting piece carries two recorded signs from which increasing or decreasing and concave up or concave down are read together. Gaps in the domain break the pieces rather than being swallowed inside a reported interval. BC-ERR-05048, partitioning at the zeros of the function itself, is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The first derivative row is correct throughout while the second derivative row is wrong on at least one piece, which is BC-SIG-05038. A different partial state builds the whole partition on the zeros of f as BC-ERR-05048 describes, so the cuts never align with the sign changes that matter. Scoring on BC-FRQ-2026-Q4-C shows the intersection step failing on its own: the union of the increasing intervals given instead of the intersection, the concave down intervals given with the increasing condition dropped, or a correct interval whose reason cites only one of the two required clauses about the plotted derivative.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An unreliable single row points to BC-SKL-05016, building a sign chart on critical points and domain boundaries, visible when even the f prime row omits a domain boundary or a point where f prime is undefined. When the f prime row is sound and only the bending row fails, the earlier skill is BC-SKL-05030, determining intervals of concavity from the sign of the second derivative.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05012 (an interval reported across an input where the function does not exist) for the conceptual failure, and BC-SKL-05016 (building the sign chart on critical points and domain boundaries) when the partition itself is the step that breaks

skills.description_formal: Partition the domain at the zeros and undefined points of f' and f'', then record both signs on each piece and read off the behaviour of f.
skills.description_plain: Record both derivative signs interval by interval.
skills.name: Build a combined sign table for the first and second derivatives

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05026 (a table of values believed to settle behaviour between the listed inputs)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: Sign changes of f prime or f double prime between tabulated inputs are reported as what the table permits, and any claim of monotonicity or concavity across a whole interval is either withheld or explicitly conditioned on an assumption stated in the response. The notation is handled cleanly, so a value of f prime at an input is distinguished from f prime as a function. BC-ERR-05049, reading a finite table as settling behaviour between the listed inputs, does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The signs in the table are read correctly and the conclusion overreaches, asserting monotonicity or concavity across an interval from three tabulated values, which is BC-SIG-05039 and BC-ERR-05049. The claim then exceeds what the data support and the justification point is unavailable even though the underlying sign reading was right.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the two rows of the table cannot be combined into a statement about f at all, the earlier skill is BC-SKL-05047, building a combined sign table for the first and second derivatives. A different tell, answering about f when the table listed f prime, is BC-PRQ-06005, reading function notation and distinguishing a function from its value at a point.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05026 (a finite table taken as a full description of the function) for the conceptual failure; misreading which object the table lists points instead to BC-PRQ-06005 (function notation, composition, and evaluation)

skills.description_formal: From selected values of f' or f'' in a table, determine sign changes, monotonicity, and concavity of f, noting what a finite table cannot settle.
skills.description_plain: Use a table of derivative values to say what the function does.
skills.name: Answer a question about a function from tabulated derivative values

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05027 (an optimisation answer is the critical point of whatever expression appears first)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every letter introduced carries a stated meaning and a unit, and the quantity to be made largest or smallest is written as an explicit formula in those letters, with the fixed relation held separately from the objective. The same naming holds whether the situation arrives as a verbal description, as a diagram, or as a table of dimensions, and the objective written matches what the question asks for rather than the first area or perimeter formula that comes to hand. Neither BC-ERR-05050 nor BC-ERR-99033 appears, so no symbol is differentiated before it has been given a meaning.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct objective formula is present but its letters are never given meanings or units, which is BC-ERR-05050 and the state recorded in BC-SIG-05040. A related partial state is BC-ERR-99033, where a symbol invented for an intermediate quantity gets used and differentiated while its connection to the quantities in the stem is left unwritten. On BC-QA-05011 this costs the setup point while later work may still proceed.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The variables are named cleanly and the formula for area, perimeter, surface area, or volume of the described figure is itself wrong or missing, or the fixed total relating two dimensions cannot be written. That points at BC-PRQ-05005 rather than at the naming step.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05027 (which quantity is being optimised and which one is fixed) for the conceptual failure; when the objective is chosen correctly and only the definitions are missing, the target is BC-ERR-05050 (writing the meaning and unit of each letter before any calculus).

skills.description_formal: From a verbal description or a diagram, define the variables with their meanings and write the quantity to be maximised or minimised in terms of them.
skills.description_plain: Say what is being made largest or smallest and label the unknowns.
skills.name: Name the quantity to be optimised and assign the variables

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05027 (an optimisation answer is the critical point of whatever expression appears first)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
adaptive.mastered_if: The constraint is solved for one variable and substituted into the objective, so what gets differentiated is a function of a single unknown. The substitution is visible on the page, the reduced objective is algebraically equivalent to the original pair, and the learner can say how many unknowns remain before taking any derivative. Across a symbolic setup and a figure based setup alike, BC-ERR-05051 is absent, meaning no expression still carrying both unknowns is sent forward to differentiation.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Objective and constraint are both written correctly, then the expression differentiated still contains both unknowns. That is BC-ERR-05051 and the not mastered observation in BC-SIG-05041. A second partial state has the substitution performed but the wrong relation treated as the fixed one, matching BC-MIS-05027, where the first expression written down is the one differentiated. On BC-QA-05011 the setup point may be earned while the derivative condition point is not.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The reduction never starts because the letters have no meanings, which is BC-SKL-05049, or because the area, perimeter, or volume relation needed for the constraint cannot be produced at all, which is BC-PRQ-05005. The tell is that no usable constraint equation exists on the page to substitute from.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05027 (telling the objective apart from the constraint) for the conceptual failure; a procedural failure, where the right constraint is identified but the algebra of solving and substituting breaks, points instead to BC-ERR-05051 (carrying out the substitution so one unknown remains).

skills.description_formal: Solve the constraint for one variable and substitute into the objective, producing a single variable function to be differentiated.
skills.description_plain: Substitute the constraint so only one unknown is left.
skills.name: Use the constraint to write the objective as a function of one variable

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05028 (the contextual domain is all inputs)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
adaptive.mastered_if: The set of inputs the situation actually allows is stated before the reduced objective is optimised, with the physical or geometric restriction named, for example that a length cannot be negative or that a dimension cannot exceed the fixed total. Whether the interval is closed is stated too, since that is what makes the boundary values legitimate candidates later. The algebraic domain of the reduced formula and the contextual domain are kept apart, and BC-ERR-05052 does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The reduced objective is optimised with no statement of which inputs the situation permits, matching BC-SIG-05042 and BC-ERR-05052, or a domain is written but taken straight from the algebra of the formula with no regard for the situation, which is BC-MIS-05028. A further partial state gives the interval without saying whether its ends are attainable, so the verification on BC-QA-05011 is left incomplete.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The domain cannot be stated because the objective was never reduced to one variable, which is BC-SKL-05050, or because the domain of a radical or rational expression cannot be determined at all, which is BC-PRQ-05003. The tell is a domain question answered about an expression that still has two unknowns in it.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05028 (what the situation permits as distinct from what the formula permits) for the conceptual failure; when the restriction is understood but the interval is written wrongly from the algebra, the target is BC-PRQ-05003 (domain of rational and radical forms).

skills.description_formal: State the set of inputs for which the reduced objective models the situation, using physical or geometric restrictions, and note whether the interval is closed.
skills.description_plain: Work out which inputs the situation actually allows.
skills.name: Determine the domain of the objective from the context

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05027 (an optimisation answer is the critical point of whatever expression appears first)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
adaptive.mastered_if: Differentiation is carried out with respect to the one variable the reduced objective actually depends on, the equation setting that derivative equal to zero is written out, and the solutions kept are the ones lying inside the contextual domain. Inputs where the derivative fails to exist are picked up as well as those where it vanishes. Work done by hand and work done on a calculator both show the equation that produced the listed inputs, so BC-ERR-05053 is absent and no variable already eliminated by the constraint is differentiated with respect to.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Correct critical inputs are listed with no equation showing the derivative set equal to zero, the state described in BC-SIG-05007, which leaves the derivative condition point on BC-QA-05011 unsupported. Another intermediate state is BC-ERR-05053, differentiation taken with respect to a variable the constraint has already removed, so the critical point is wrong even though the procedure looks complete. Candidates outside the contextual interval may also be retained.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The derivative is taken of an expression that still contains both unknowns, which is a failure of BC-SKL-05050 rather than of this step, or critical points are not recognised as the inputs where f prime is zero or undefined, which is BC-SKL-05010.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05027 (knowing which expression is the one to differentiate) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, where the right function is differentiated but the equation and its solutions are mishandled, points to BC-SKL-05010 (critical points where the first derivative equals zero).

skills.description_formal: Differentiate the reduced objective, set the derivative equal to zero, and retain the solutions inside the contextual domain.
skills.description_plain: Take the derivative of the objective and find where it is zero or undefined.
skills.name: Differentiate the objective and solve for critical points

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05018 (a local test settles a global question)
BC-MIS-05029 (finding a critical point finishes an optimisation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
adaptive.mastered_if: After the critical point is found, an argument follows that closes the question of which extremum it gives, and the response names which argument it used. On a closed contextual domain that means the candidates test with the objective evaluated at every interior critical input and at both ends, values compared in writing. Where the domain is not closed and there is exactly one critical point, the sole critical point rule is invoked by name with the sign behaviour of f prime on each side stated. BC-ERR-05054 and BC-ERR-99004 are both absent, so no vanishing derivative is reported as an extremum on its own and no local sign change stands in for a global claim.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative is set to zero, solved, and the value announced as the maximum or minimum with nothing in between, which is BC-ERR-05054 and BC-SIG-05043. Closer to mastery is BC-ERR-99004, where a verification is attempted but stays local, a single sign change offered for an absolute claim, or a candidates test run with an endpoint or an interior critical input left out. Both leave the verification point on BC-QA-05011 unearned while the answer point can survive.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The candidate itself is wrong because the derivative work failed, which is BC-SKL-05052, or a correct global argument cannot be written for any problem, which is BC-SKL-05028, or the sole critical point route is unavailable because extending a relative extremum to an absolute one is not held, which is BC-SKL-05038.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05029 (a vanishing derivative is not yet an answer) for the conceptual failure; when verification is attempted but stays local, the target is BC-SKL-05028 (writing a global justification covering every candidate).

skills.description_formal: Close the argument with the candidates test on a closed contextual domain, or with the sole critical point rule, and state which was used.
skills.description_plain: Show the critical point really is the maximum or minimum wanted.
skills.name: Verify that the critical point gives the required extremum on the domain

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05030 (a numerical answer is a complete interpretation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
adaptive.mastered_if: Three things arrive together in the final line, the extreme value of the objective, the units of the quantity being modelled, and the input at which it occurs. Units are built from the modelled quantity rather than copied from the variable, so an optimal volume is reported in cubic units and not in the units of a length. Whether the arithmetic was done by hand or on a calculator, the reported number is the value of the objective and not the value of the input, and neither BC-ERR-05055 nor BC-ERR-99005 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct number stands alone in an applied context with no unit attached, the observation in BC-SIG-05044 and the error BC-ERR-05055. Related is BC-ERR-99005, units present but built from the original quantity instead of the derived one. A third intermediate state reports value and units but omits the input at which the extremum occurs, so the interpreted value point on BC-QA-05011 is only partly supported.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: There is nothing correct to report because the extremum was never verified, which is BC-SKL-05053. The tell is a confidently reported optimum whose status as a maximum rather than a minimum was never settled.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05030 (a number by itself does not report an optimum) for the conceptual failure; a procedural failure where units are attempted but assembled wrongly points to BC-ERR-99005 (building the units of the derived quantity).

skills.description_formal: State the extreme value of the objective together with the units of the modelled quantity and the input at which the extremum occurs.
skills.description_plain: Give the best value, its units, and where it happens.
skills.name: Report the optimal value with its units and the input where it occurs

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05030 (a numerical answer is a complete interpretation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
adaptive.mastered_if: A sentence in words carries the modelled quantity by name, its units, and the input at which the extremum occurs, and it reads correctly to someone who never sees the algebra above it. The sentence says which way the extremum goes, largest or smallest, and it answers the question that was asked rather than a neighbouring one. BC-ERR-05056 and BC-ERR-99027 are both absent, so no number is interpreted without saying what it measures and when it is attained.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sentence names the modelled quantity but drops either the units or the input where the extremum occurs, which is BC-SIG-05045 and BC-ERR-05056. BC-ERR-99027 covers the wider version, an interpretation written without the interval named or answering a different question than the one asked. The interpretation point on BC-QA-05011 needs the whole set of phrases, so a sentence missing one of them does not earn it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sentence has nothing complete to draw on because the value, its units, and the input were never assembled in the first place, which is BC-SKL-05054. The tell is an interpretation attempt built around a bare number.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05030 (what a complete statement about the situation has to contain) for the conceptual failure; when the parts are all known but the sentence assembles them incompletely, the target is BC-ERR-99027 (naming the quantity, the units, and the input in one sentence).

skills.description_formal: Write a sentence naming the modelled quantity, its units, and the input at which the extremum occurs, so that the sentence stands without the algebra.
skills.description_plain: Say in words what the number means for the thing being modelled.
skills.name: Interpret the optimal value as a statement about the situation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05028 (the contextual domain is all inputs)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both ends of the contextual interval are evaluated in the objective whenever they are attainable, their values are written down next to the interior candidate values, and the comparison itself appears in the conclusion rather than being left implied. Where an endpoint is not attainable, that is said and the reason given, so the omission is a stated decision and not a gap. BC-ERR-05026 and BC-ERR-99004 are both absent, meaning no candidate comparison skips an endpoint and no local derivative test is offered where the comparison was required.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The answer comes out right and the justification is a first or second derivative test at the candidate, which is BC-SIG-05021 and the local argument described in BC-ERR-99004. A narrower version is BC-ERR-05026, a candidates comparison made over the interior critical points only, with one or both ends never evaluated. The 2023 guideline withholds the justification point from a response that does not consider both endpoints.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: There are no endpoints to check because the contextual interval was never determined, which is BC-SKL-05051, or the habit of comparing every candidate in one written argument is missing generally, which is BC-SKL-05028.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05028 (why the allowed range and its ends matter to the answer) for the conceptual failure; when the interval is stated correctly and the ends are simply not evaluated, the target is BC-SKL-05028 (a global justification covering every candidate).

skills.description_formal: Evaluate the objective at the boundary of the contextual domain, where that boundary is attainable, and include the comparison in the reported conclusion.
skills.description_plain: Compare the interior candidate with the ends of the allowed range.
skills.name: Check the optimum against the endpoints of the contextual domain

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05015 (the location of an extremum and its value are treated as the same answer)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05011 (applied optimisation with model setup, domain, and verification)
adaptive.mastered_if: The closing line of an applied optimisation answers the demand that was actually written, so when the question asks for the minimum cost the response states that cost with its units, and when it asks for the dimensions it states the input values instead. Work on both the table setup and the verbal context version of BC-QA-05011 shows the same habit, the extreme value and the input where it occurs are written as two separate labelled quantities, and BC-ERR-05024 (naming the location when the value was asked for, or the reverse) does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: All the optimisation machinery runs correctly and only the final reporting misses, which is BC-SIG-05017, where the extremum is located properly and then the input is handed in as the answer to a question about the value. BC-ERR-05024 shows up in exactly this shape, and the 2023 guideline under BC-QA-05011 gave the answer point only for the minimum value, so a response can carry the setup, the derivative condition and the verification and still lose the last point.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the response never separates the two quantities anywhere in the work, the failure sits in BC-SKL-05054 (report the optimal value with its units and the input where it occurs) rather than in reading the question, and the tell is that neither units nor an input label appear on the final line at all.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05015 (input at which the extremum occurs versus the extreme value itself) for the conceptual failure; a response that holds the distinction but still reports the wrong one under time pressure points instead to BC-SKL-05054 (reporting the optimal value with its units and the input where it occurs)

skills.description_formal: Read the demand of the question and report either the extreme value of the objective or the values of the variables that produce it, as asked.
skills.description_plain: Return the thing the question wanted, value or dimensions.
skills.name: Answer the question asked in an applied optimisation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05031 (a relation has critical points only where its derivative is zero)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05012 (critical points and second derivative behaviour of an implicit relation)
adaptive.mastered_if: Horizontal tangents on an implicit relation come from setting the numerator of dy/dx to zero, and the denominator is evaluated at each candidate before it is kept. Discarded candidates are named and the reason is written down, that the denominator vanishes there so no tangent exists, and the surviving solutions are carried into the defining relation. Across the BC-QA-05012 path the derivative is differentiated implicitly rather than as though y were free, and BC-ERR-05057 (points reported where the denominator also vanishes) is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Numerator equals zero is solved correctly and the denominator is never looked at, which is BC-SIG-05046, so points where both parts vanish are listed as horizontal tangents. That is BC-ERR-05057, and the critical point list comes out wrong even though the implicit differentiation earned its point. The BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-C commentary records the neighbouring behaviour where the whole derivative expression was set to zero, denominator included.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the candidate equation itself is mis-solved, or the denominator is not recognised as an object that can vanish, the gap is BC-PRQ-05001 (solving equations and inequalities to locate where an expression is zero or undefined), and the sign of it is a factored expression handled correctly in one factor and dropped in another. A failure to combine the candidate with the curve equation points to BC-PRQ-05007 instead, and shaky dy/dx to begin with points to BC-SKL-03014.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05031 (only the numerator is treated as carrying critical point information) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure in solving or in the denominator check points instead to BC-PRQ-05001 (locating where an expression is zero or undefined)

skills.description_formal: Set the numerator of dy/dx equal to zero, keep only points where the denominator is nonzero, and solve together with the defining relation.
skills.description_plain: Find the points on the curve with a horizontal tangent.
skills.name: Determine where the derivative of an implicit relation equals zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05031 (a relation has critical points only where its derivative is zero)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05012 (critical points and second derivative behaviour of an implicit relation)
adaptive.mastered_if: Vertical tangents are treated as a second family of critical points with their own condition, the denominator of dy/dx equal to zero, and every solution of that equation is then tested in the defining relation before it is reported. Coordinates that fail the relation are struck out in the work. On the BC-QA-05012 curve the response states in words that the derivative fails to exist at the surviving points, and BC-ERR-05058 (denominator solutions reported without a matching point on the curve) never appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05047 is the visible state here, the denominator equation is solved and its solutions are listed without substituting them back into the relation. BC-ERR-05058 follows, the reported coordinates are unsupported because nothing shows they lie on the curve. A related partial state is looking only at the numerator so the vertical tangent family is never raised at all, which is what BC-MIS-05031 describes.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the denominator equation and the relation are never combined into one system, the earlier gap is BC-PRQ-05007 (solving a system made of a defining relation and a derived equation), and the tell is a list of bare input values with no attempt at the paired outputs. Trouble finding where the denominator vanishes at all belongs to BC-PRQ-05001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05031 (the denominator of the derivative carries no critical point information) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure in checking candidates against the relation points instead to BC-PRQ-05007 (solving the defining relation together with a derived equation)

skills.description_formal: Set the denominator of dy/dx equal to zero, solve together with the defining relation, and record those points as critical points.
skills.description_plain: Find the points on the curve with a vertical tangent.
skills.name: Determine where the derivative of an implicit relation fails to exist

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05032 (a single coordinate is taken to name a point on a relation)
BC-MIS-05031 (a relation has critical points only where its derivative is zero)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05012 (critical points and second derivative behaviour of an implicit relation)
adaptive.mastered_if: Two equations are held at once, the derived condition and the defining relation, and the substitution produces coordinate pairs rather than a bare input. Each reported answer is an ordered pair that satisfies the relation, and where one input pairs with two outputs both are listed or one is ruled out with a stated reason. The same pairing discipline holds whether the curve arrives as an equation in two variables or as a differential equation, and BC-ERR-05059 (one coordinate handed in where a point was asked for) is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The system is solved and the answer stops one step short, which BC-SIG-05048 records as an input value given where a point on the curve was wanted. BC-ERR-05059 names the same behaviour and its cost, the answer is incomplete because the relation may pass through several outputs at that input. A second partial state is finding one of the pair of outputs and not noticing the other.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A candidate condition that was wrong before the substitution began means the gap is upstream in BC-SKL-05058 (where dy/dx equals zero) or BC-SKL-05059 (where dy/dx fails to exist), and the tell is that the substitution is carried out cleanly on an equation that should never have been formed. Difficulty with the elimination itself belongs to BC-PRQ-05007.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05032 (an input value treated as a point on a relation) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure inside the elimination points instead to BC-PRQ-05007 (solving a system made of a defining relation and a derived equation)

skills.description_formal: Substitute the derived condition into the defining relation and solve the resulting system for the coordinates of the critical point.
skills.description_plain: Use both equations to get the actual point on the curve.
skills.name: Solve the defining relation and the derived condition together

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05033 (implicit differentiation may treat the dependent variable as a constant)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05012 (critical points and second derivative behaviour of an implicit relation)
adaptive.mastered_if: Differentiating dy/dx a second time, every appearance of the dependent variable picks up its chain rule factor, so the quotient or product rule is applied and the resulting expression contains x, y, and dy/dx together rather than x alone. The derivative symbol is left in place at this stage instead of being quietly dropped. Work on the BC-QA-05012 path shows the second differentiation earning its own point, and BC-ERR-05060 (the second variable treated as a constant) does not occur.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05049 marks the state where the chain rule factor on the dependent variable is missing from the second differentiation, which is BC-ERR-05060. The differentiation point is lost, though the record notes the value point stays reachable through a correct substitution afterwards. A milder partial state keeps the chain rule but mishandles the quotient rule bookkeeping on the way.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the first derivative expression was never produced or verified correctly, the failure is BC-SKL-03014 (verify a supplied expression for dy/dx by implicit differentiation), and the tell is that the chain rule is also missing from the first differentiation, not only the second. Trouble carrying the relation alongside the derived equation points to BC-PRQ-05007.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05033 (the dependent variable differentiated as though it were constant) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure in the product and quotient bookkeeping points instead to BC-SKL-03014 (verifying a supplied dy/dx by implicit differentiation)

skills.description_formal: Differentiate dy/dx with respect to x using the product, quotient, and chain rules, producing an expression in x, y, and dy/dx.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate the derivative expression again, keeping both variables.
skills.name: Compute a second derivative of an implicit relation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05033 (implicit differentiation may treat the dependent variable as a constant)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05012 (critical points and second derivative behaviour of an implicit relation)
adaptive.mastered_if: A number is asked for and a number is delivered. The value of dy/dx at the point, or its expression, replaces every occurrence of the derivative symbol in the second derivative expression, then the coordinates go in, and the final answer carries no dy/dx anywhere. Lines of work are joined only where the two sides are genuinely equal, so a general expression in x and y is not written equal to its value at one point. Neither BC-ERR-05061 (first derivative left unsubstituted) nor BC-ERR-99002 (unequal objects joined by an equals sign) appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The reported second derivative still carries the first derivative symbol inside it, which is BC-SIG-05050 and BC-ERR-05061, and the substitution point is lost while the differentiation point survives, since the 2025 guideline treats the two as separate points. The other intermediate state is presentational, BC-ERR-99002, where the expression and its numerical value are strung together with equals signs and the presentation or setup credit goes.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the expression being substituted into is itself missing the chain rule factor on the dependent variable, the gap is BC-SKL-05061 (compute a second derivative of an implicit relation), and the tell is that the substitution is executed carefully on an expression that has no dy/dx in it to substitute for.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05033 (the derivative symbol left standing as though it needed no value) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure in the arithmetic of the substitution or in the equals sign chain points instead to BC-SKL-05061 (computing the second derivative of the relation)

skills.description_formal: Replace dy/dx in the second derivative expression by its value or its expression at the point, then substitute the coordinates to obtain the numerical second derivative.
skills.description_plain: Put the value of the first derivative back in to get a number.
skills.name: Substitute the derivative expression to evaluate a second derivative at a point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05023 (the second derivative test always decides)
BC-MIS-05033 (implicit differentiation may treat the dependent variable as a constant)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05012 (critical points and second derivative behaviour of an implicit relation)
BC-QA-05013 (second derivative test applied at a critical point)
adaptive.mastered_if: Classification on a relation starts by confirming that dy/dx is zero at the point, moves to the evaluated second derivative there, and reads a negative value as a relative maximum and a positive value as a relative minimum, stated in that direction in words. A second derivative of zero is reported as inconclusive rather than forced into a verdict. The reasoning travels between the implicit curve of BC-QA-05012 and the plain critical point of BC-QA-05013, and BC-ERR-05062 (correct number, reversed classification) is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05028 captures the common near miss, the numerical second derivative is right and the extremum type announced is the opposite one, which is BC-ERR-05062. A second intermediate state is treating the test as always decisive, so a zero second derivative is read as a verdict. The BC-QA-05013 record also notes that this justification was accepted in 2024 but refused in 2025 where a global demand was made, so a locally correct argument can still miss the justification point.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A wrong sign that traces back to the evaluation rather than the reading means the gap is BC-SKL-05062 (substitute the derivative expression to evaluate a second derivative at a point), and the tell is a second derivative value that still depends on an unsubstituted dy/dx. If the sign to classification mapping fails on ordinary functions as well, the gap is BC-SKL-05036 (apply the second derivative test at a critical point).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05023 (the test read as always decisive, including at a zero second derivative) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure where the sign is computed correctly and mapped backwards points instead to BC-SKL-05036 (applying the second derivative test at a critical point)

skills.description_formal: At a point where dy/dx is zero, use the sign of the evaluated second derivative to classify the point as a relative maximum or a relative minimum on the relation.
skills.description_plain: Use the sign of the second derivative at the point to call it a high or low point.
skills.name: Classify a critical point of an implicit relation using the second derivative
